A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOOP research work and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures and references. Comparison covers all 16 pages of v5 and 23 pages of v7, including v7 Appendices A–F; v5 has no appendix section.

before.justification: Sections 7–8 report original diffusion fine-tuning experiments, training curves, validation rewards and generated-image examples.

after.justification: Original training and validation results remain, with additional comparator experiments, ablations, computational measurements and diversity results in Appendices B–F.

M1.justification: LOOP retains multiple trajectories per prompt, the leave-one-out baseline and clipped importance-sampling updates in Equations 13–14. The omissions of KL regularization and standard-deviation normalization also remain; Appendix A supplies pseudocode without establishing an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate color, shape, texture, spatial relations, numeracy, aesthetics and image–text alignment. The added appendix experiments examine retained tasks; the auxiliary model fork and four selected aesthetic prompts do not establish new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix B adds an evaluated GRPO comparator in a small-scale aesthetic experiment; v5 discussed GRPO without comparing it experimentally. Appendices C–D add baseline-choice and unclipped-PPO comparisons, while the main benchmark comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New auxiliary protocols use an unofficial Stable Diffusion fork in Appendices B–C, measure runtime and peak memory in Appendix E, and evaluate pairwise CLIP diversity across four prompts in Appendix F. The stated main training and validation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained trajectory-count study and qualitative examples, v7 adds running-mean versus leave-one-out baseline analysis, an isolated clipping ablation, runtime/memory profiling and reward–diversity analysis. Appendices C–F substantially expand evidence concerning the method’s mechanisms and practical trade-offs.

E5.justification: v5 reported three-run training averages with 80% prediction intervals but point estimates in Tables 1–3. v7 adds three-run standard deviations to the experimental table results and changes Figures 2–3 shading to ±1 standard deviation. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds LOOP k=2 results, while Table 3 changes reported means: DDPO aesthetic reward changes from 6.8135 to 6.6795 and LOOP k=4 from 7.8606 to 7.7061. New comparator, ablation, runtime and diversity results substantially extend the evidence. Figure 3 also changes the alignment curves and scale without explaining the basis, preventing a reliable same-setting performance interpretation.

T1.justification: v7 introduces a LOOP-specific formal variance guarantee through Proposition 4.1 and its proof, asserting strictly lower variance than PPO with 1/K^2 scaling. v5 contained variance-reduction motivation but no corresponding proposition; the existing state-distribution definitions and Theorem 3.1 remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the central efficiency claim from computational efficiency versus performance to sample efficiency measured by training prompts. v7 explicitly acknowledges additional sampling cost and leaves computational-efficiency improvement to future work, materially narrowing the principal claim.

C2.justification: v7 adds online/offline applicability distinctions, a policy-drift explanation for running-mean baseline weaknesses, and interpretations connecting multiple trajectories to exploration and diversity. Appendix F claims joint reward/diversity improvement and consistently lowest diversity for PPO, although Figure 11 contains counterexamples, including the octopus panel.

D1.justification: v7 newly specifies DDIM sampling with eta=1.0, provides LOOP pseudocode, explains DDPO’s running-mean baseline, and supplies checkpoint-access information for auxiliary experiments. Runtime and memory measurements are added; the previously stated optimizer, batch size, hardware and core hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: New Section 2.5 develops the relationship to offline preference-based diffusion alignment and explains the absence of direct DPO comparisons. Additional references include Gambashidze et al., Kang et al. and Venkatraman et al.; the main positioning relative to GRPO was already present in v5.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify efficiency terminology and method motivation, correct the section roadmap, and update author/publication information and acknowledgements. Section 2.5 and appendices are added, while the existing Sections 1–9 sequence and much of their prose remain.

P2.justification: v7 adds pseudocode Figure 6 and analytical Figures 7–11, expands the tables for uncertainty reporting, and redraws/enlarges training plots. Existing qualitative images are retained with layout edits. New display inconsistencies include Figure 8’s GRPO caption for a baseline-choice comparison and Figure 3’s apparently duplicated color/alignment panels.

improvement.justification: v7 improves uncertainty reporting, computational-cost disclosure and experimental controls, while narrowing the efficiency claim. However, Proposition 4.1’s new 1/K^2 proof neglects variance summation and shared-baseline dependence; Figure 3 apparently repeats the color curves for alignment; and Appendix F’s diversity interpretation contradicts Figure 11, where LOOP k=4 has the lowest octopus diversity. Substantial reporting gains coexist with new errors affecting theoretical and empirical conclusions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
